findings.issue: 勝つ means 'to win', not 'to earn' (likely back-translated from ambiguous pt 'ganhar'). The literal field teaches a wrong verb meaning; token gloss and en correctly say 'win'.

tokens[0]-[3] (小, 学校, 思い, だす — all fields null) are stray duplicated fragments prepended before the real tokenization, which starts at 小学校. They duplicate parts of 小学校 and 思いだす and corrupt surface concatenation/alignment.
findings.current: 小 / 学校 / 思い / だす (four all-null stray tokens before 小学校)
findings.suggested: Delete tokens 0-3; the token list should start at 小学校.

findings.issue: 以前ほど…ない is an extent comparison ('not as fat as before'), not a より comparison. 'Hasn't gotten fatter than before' changes the semantics (could mean equally fat) and contradicts en/pt/expl.
findings.current: As for him, he hasn't gotten fatter than before.
findings.suggested: As for him, (he) is not fat to the extent of before.

findings.issue: 拾った means 'picked (it) up / found', not 'caught'; and 海岸で belongs inside the quoted clause (expl says the quoted clause is 海岸で拾った), but here 'on the beach' sits outside the quote, reading as where the saying happens.
findings.current: He's saying 'I caught it,' on the beach.
findings.suggested: He's saying, 'I picked it up on the beach.'

findings.issue: The en drops the hearsay conveyed by んだって, which is the sentence's key grammar point; pt ('Disseram que...'), lit_en and both expl fields all convey the reported-information nuance.
findings.suggested: I hear she hasn't decided yet.

findings.issue: In いっぱい勝ちたい, いっぱい is a quantity adverb ('a lot, plenty'), matching role 'advérbio de quantidade' and pt 'bastante, muito'. 'quite, very' is a degree gloss that does not fit this sentence (*'I want to win very').

After the noun 必要, ない is the i-adjective predicate ('there is no ~'), not an auxiliary; the auxiliary ない attaches to verb stems. The token's own note correctly calls it 形容詞 ない, so the role contradicts the note.
findings.suggested: adjetivo predicativo de negação (形容詞 ない)

findings.issue: この means only 'this' (near speaker); 'that' belongs to その/あの. Including 'that' teaches a false fact about the ko-so-a-do system.
